title: RBH17 4-round AES / aes-4r-yoyo-rbh2017

target.description: 4 nonlinear AES rounds in the source enck/deck convention, omitting initial ShiftRows and final ShiftRows/MixColumns. Section 3 explains public linear conjugation to full-round AES.

setting.key_relation: One unknown standard AES master key and its expanded round keys.
setting.plaintext_model: Yoyo swap-generated adaptive encryption/decryption texts under one unknown key; the source native chosen-text count is not automatically an aggregate oracle-call count.
setting.reference_model: Adaptive bidirectional secret-key distinguishing versus a random permutation and its inverse; no known-key or related-key oracle.

time.note: Source Table 2 records two XOR observations; oracle executions and external-linear transformations are not included.

data.note: Two encryptions and two adaptively chosen decryptions.

memory.note: No numerical resource amount supplied for this endpoint.

preprocessing.note: No numerical resource amount supplied for this endpoint.

success.description: The source yoyo test accepts AES with probability 1 for its valid nontrivial constructed pairs under the stated linear-layer convention. This is AES-side acceptance, not a numerical equal-prior two-sided classification probability.

review.scope: Checked the deterministic zero-pattern relation and source test algorithm, including valid nontrivial swap conditions; random-permutation events are kept separate.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.4–5 Table 2 and native units; pp.12–16 Section 3 linear-layer convention and Sections 3.1–3.2 Algorithms 2–3.
evidence.interpretation: Targeted primary result statements and accounting checked; not a complete-paper proof audit.

evidence.locator: Complete PDF1–27 / printed217–243, all sections, algorithms, cost paragraphs and references.
evidence.interpretation: Complete exact-primary inventory, with independent consequential-section review. No author attack code executed.

evidence.locator: PDF8/printed224 Theorem2; PDF15–16/printed231–232 Section3.2/Algorithm3; PDF13 nontrivial swaps and linear wrappers.
evidence.interpretation: Theoretical acceptance of the exact source test; no imported random-side error probability and no secret-key recovery claim.

limitations: Requires adaptive encryption and decryption under the same unknown key, with the source-defined round boundary.
